clue.text: Very keen to have a look into god

indicators.note: 'into' asks for the words before it to be put inside the word after it

parts.note: Zeus is the king of the Greek gods
lo, as in 'lo and behold', is an old call to look

explanation.surface: Someone is desperate to catch a glimpse of a deity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Have a look into' reads like peering at a god, but 'into' only says where the pieces go.
explanation.definitionFit: Zealous describes a person full of fervour and enthusiasm for a cause.

clue.text: After the start of expansion Nato is changing this country

indicators.note: the start of a word is just its opening letter
letters that are changing are being rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A Baltic state was transformed after NATO began its eastward expansion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' places the rearranged NATO IS after E. Estonia did join NATO in its 2004 expansion, so the answer fits the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Estonia is a Baltic nation in northern Europe, bordering Latvia and Russia.

clue.text: Nigella gelatinised revolting stuffing — that's valid!

indicators.note: revolting here means turning over, so the letters are read backwards
stuffing is what sits inside, so the letters are found inside the phrase

parts.note: found across the end of Nigella and the start of gelatinised

explanation.surface: Nigella Lawson's gelatine-set filling looks disgusting, yet she insists it's acceptable.
explanation.walkthrough: Nigella Lawson is a well-known British TV cook. 'Revolting' looks like a verdict on the food but signals reading backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Something legal is lawful and therefore valid in the eyes of the law.

clue.text: Dislodges mixed nuts, swallowing large amount of water

indicators.note: swallowing means taking something in, so one piece goes inside the other
letters that are mixed are jumbled into another order

parts.note: a sea is a large body of water

explanation.surface: Someone shakes loose a mixture of nuts while gulping a lot of water.
explanation.definitionFit: To unseat is to remove someone from a seat or position, as a horse throws its rider.

clue.text: Europeans declared money orders

indicators.note: something declared is spoken out, so we go by the sound of the word

parts.note: Czechs are people from the Czech Republic

explanation.surface: Some Europeans announced their banking instructions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Declared' reads like a customs declaration but signals that the answer sounds like the people.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheque is a written order to a bank to pay a sum of money to someone.

clue.text: Got better chief to hold the Spanish back

indicators.note: to hold something is to keep it inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: the head is the chief person

indicators.note: going back means the word is read from right to left

explanation.surface: A boss recovered by keeping the Spaniards at bay.
explanation.definitionFit: Healed is the past tense of heal, meaning recovered from injury or illness.

clue.text: French who sleep I largely call confused

indicators.note: largely means most but not all, so the last letter is cut off

explanation.surface: A Frenchman who is half asleep makes a muddled phone call.
explanation.definitionFit: A quizzical look shows puzzlement, the expression of someone who is baffled.

clue.text: Highest point for serviette without it disintegrating

indicators.note: something disintegrating falls apart, so its letters are scattered into a new order
without means lacking, so those letters are taken away

parts.note: a serviette is a table napkin

explanation.surface: A napkin falling to pieces is the peak of bad dining.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking I and T from SERVIETTE leaves SERVETE, which rearranges into the mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: Mount Everest is the tallest mountain on Earth, the world's loftiest summit.

clue.text: If girls get involved with that FC it'll be a stop-go situation

indicators.note: letters that get involved become tangled together and come out in another order

explanation.surface: If women start dating players from a football club, the relationship will be on-again, off-again.
explanation.walkthrough: FC is football club. 'Stop-go situation' sounds like a fitful romance but describes signals at a junction.
explanation.definitionFit: Traffic lights tell drivers when to halt and when to proceed, alternating between red and green.

clue.text: Street silver for blokes

definitions.note: adjective: as in a stag party, for men only

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A road paved with silver, meant only for men.
explanation.walkthrough: A bloke is a man; a stag night is a party for a groom and his male friends.
explanation.definitionFit: Stag describes an event attended only by men, especially a pre-wedding night out.

clue.text: Disraeli prepared to tour Home Counties one bit at a time

indicators.note: to tour a place is to go around it, so one piece wraps around the other
prepared means worked into shape, so the letters are reworked into a new arrangement

parts.note: the Home Counties lie in the South East of England, abbreviated SE

explanation.surface: Victorian prime minister Disraeli got ready for a gradual campaign around the counties near London.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties surrounding London. Disraeli was also a novelist, and Victorian novels were often published in instalments.
explanation.definitionFit: A serialised story is published in instalments, appearing piece by piece over successive issues.

clue.text: Fashion gala in Olde England

indicators.note: to fashion something is to shape it, so the letters are shaped into a new order

explanation.surface: A costume event set in a mock-medieval English village.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fashion gala' reads as a catwalk event; 'in' belongs to the letters, not the link.
explanation.definitionFit: Anglia is the Latin name for England, used in older and historical writing.

clue.text: Cooked incorporating Zen, perhaps, or its opposite!

indicators.note: incorporating means taking into the body, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: fried food has been cooked in fat

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the word is only one possible arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: A dish made with calm Zen ingredients, or perhaps the very reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points back to Zen: the opposite of Zen calm is wild agitation.
explanation.definitionFit: Zen suggests serene calm, and frenzied means wildly agitated, its direct contrary.

clue.text: Fiats can't crash? That's unbelievable!

indicators.note: in a crash things get smashed up, so the letters are wrecked into another order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Someone claims that Fiat cars never crash, and a listener scoffs.
explanation.definitionFit: Fantastic can mean fanciful or incredible, too strange to be true.

clue.text: Label paintings put up on loan finally out of Denmark

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting something up means writing it bottom to top
out of means removed from, so that letter is taken away
finally points to the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A gallery tag for pictures hung on loan from Denmark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put up' and 'on loan' suggest an exhibition, but they reverse a word and pick a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A trademark is a registered brand name or logo, a label identifying a maker's goods.

clue.text: A nice kind of accent

explanation.surface: Someone admires a charming way of speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Accent' suggests speech, but it is the written mark over a letter, as in é.
explanation.definitionFit: The acute is a diacritic sloping up to the right, used over vowels in French.

clue.text: Islander's copper prohibition

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A man from an island faces a ban on copper.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cuban is a native of Cuba, the largest island in the Caribbean.

clue.text: Leaders of Ukraine never had strong desire to be free from attachment

indicators.note: the leaders of a group of words are their opening letters

parts.note: first letters of the three words

explanation.surface: Ukraine's rulers never longed for independence from a powerful neighbour.
explanation.definitionFit: To unhitch is to unfasten or detach, as when releasing a trailer or horse.

clue.text: Innocent and feeble in praise

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the first piece goes within the second

parts.note: to bless is to praise, especially God
a lame excuse is a feeble one

explanation.surface: Someone guileless and weak in commending others.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone blameless has done nothing wrong and deserves no fault.

clue.text: Found in caramel, an incredible colour

indicators.note: found in means the letters can be located inside the phrase that follows

parts.note: spans the end of caramel, all of an, and the start of incredible

explanation.surface: A cook marvels at the amazing shade of caramel.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma after caramel is ignored when reading through.
explanation.definitionFit: Melanin is the dark pigment giving skin, hair and eyes their tint.

clue.text: In addition, bird has a breastbone

indicators.note: to have something is to hold it, so the first piece holds the second

explanation.surface: Besides everything else, the bird has a prominent chest bone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In addition' looks like 'also', but it is SUM, an addition, which has the bird inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The sternum is the flat bone at the front of the chest joining the ribs.

clue.text: Slowly undressing, lady bags Dior

indicators.note: undressing strips off the outer layers, so each word loses its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A woman takes her time disrobing, clutching her Dior designer handbag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bags' looks like a verb but is just another word to strip. Adagio is a musical tempo marking.
explanation.definitionFit: Adagio is the Italian musical direction meaning at a leisurely, unhurried tempo.

clue.text: Herder: 'Say nothing terribly deep or grand, initially'

parts.note: sh is what you say to ask for silence

indicators.note: terribly suggests something badly done, so the letters are thrown into disorder
initially points to the first letter of each word

parts.note: first letters of or and grand

explanation.surface: A shepherd is told to keep quiet and avoid anything too profound or lofty.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheepdog is trained to round up and drive a flock of sheep.

clue.text: Youngsters producing rubbish

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a brood of animals born together
second meaning: waste dropped in a public place

explanation.walkthrough: 'Producing' makes it sound like children make a mess; it only joins the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both newborn animals delivered at one birth and discarded refuse in the street.

clue.text: Quintet for river dweller

definitions.note: a proper name: Schubert's Quintet in A major
definitions.meaning: first meaning: the popular name of a Schubert chamber piece for five players

explanation.walkthrough: Schubert's Piano Quintet takes its nickname from a song about a fish, whose melody it borrows.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a speckled freshwater fish and also Schubert's famous chamber work for five instruments.

clue.text: The ratings are misleading: fix what's bent

indicators.note: something misleading is twisted out of its true form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A complaint that viewing figures are deceptive, with a demand to correct the crooked numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bent' can mean dishonest, which fits the rigged-ratings story, but here it simply means not straight.
explanation.definitionFit: To straighten something is to remove its curves or kinks so it runs true.

clue.text: Acknowledges dresses no good

indicators.note: no means without, so that letter is dropped

explanation.surface: Someone admits their frocks are no good.
explanation.definitionFit: To own up to something is to admit it, as in 'he owns that he was wrong'.

clue.text: Agree with boy eating fish

indicators.note: eating takes something inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a son is a boy child

explanation.surface: A parent consents to a lad having a fish supper.
explanation.definitionFit: To shake on a deal is to seal an agreement with a handshake.

clue.text: Tiny part in any field of study

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the first piece goes within the second

parts.note: an atom is a tiny particle

explanation.surface: Every discipline has its minute details.
explanation.definitionFit: Anatomy is the branch of science dealing with the bodily structure of organisms.
